theme: 3 terms for data in SwiftUI: the stored value, the link to it and the single owner

terms.definition: A property wrapper that lets a view store a value and redraw when it changes.
terms.example: Store the counter in State, so the screen updates.

terms.definition: A two-way link to a value that another view owns.
terms.example: Pass a Binding to the child view, so it can edit the name.

terms.definition: The one place that owns a value, so every other view reads it from there.
terms.example: The parent view is the Source of Truth for the name.

video.title: State, Binding & Source of Truth | Day 135
video.description:
Learn to explain how a SwiftUI view keeps and shares a value: State, Binding & Source of Truth, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
State - A property wrapper that lets a view store a value and redraw when it changes.
Binding - A two-way link to a value that another view owns.
Source of Truth - The one place that owns a value, so every other view reads it from there.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain State, Binding & Source of Truth in SwiftUI by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

State - A property wrapper that lets a view store a value and redraw when it changes.
한국어: 스테이트: 뷰가 값을 저장하고 값이 바뀌면 화면을 다시 그리게 하는 프로퍼티 래퍼

Binding - A two-way link to a value that another view owns.

한국어: 소스 오브 트루스: 값을 하나만 소유해서 다른 모든 뷰가 그곳에서 읽게 하는 유일한 장소

landscape.hook: Can you explain State, Binding and Source of Truth in English?

dialogue.title: The sound switch

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I want the sound switch to remember its value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Store it in State, like `isOn` in the code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A struct cannot change its own properties. State keeps the value outside, and SwiftUI redraws when it changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And what is the `$` in front of `isOn`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It creates a Binding. A Binding lets the Toggle read and write `isOn`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Toggle has its own copy?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. That is the Source of Truth rule: one owner, and everyone else gets a Binding.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I made a second State for the same switch in a child view. It broke.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now you have two copies, so there is no single Source of Truth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I will delete it and pass a Binding down instead.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. State at the top, Binding below.
Store the value in State, and the screen updates.
